chunks: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about Allah, can He be described? He said: Do you not read the Quran? I said: Yes. He said: Do you not read His words the Exalted: 'Sights do not encompass Him, while He encompasses sights'? I said: Yes. He said: Do you know what 'sights' means? I said: The sight of the eyes. He said: The imaginings of the hearts are greater than the sight of the eyes, so He is not encompassed by the imaginings, while He encompasses the imaginings.

key_terms.أَوْهَامُ: imaginings, conjectures, or mental perceptions (plural of wahm)

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Rida explain the limits of human perception regarding God's essence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of divine transcendence (tanzih) by distinguishing between physical sight and mental imagination, noting that if eyes cannot grasp God, the 'awham' (imaginings/conceptions) of the heart are even more limited. This hadith is foundational in Shia theology for refuting anthropomorphism (tashbih) and clarifying that while God is knowable, His essence remains beyond full human comprehension. The dialogue underscores that divine reality exceeds both sensory perception and cognitive representation.

en.ammaar-muslim: 6. [6/325] al-Kafi: Muhammad b. Yahya from Ahmad b. Muhammad from Abi Hashim al-Ja’fari from Abi al-Hasan al-Ridha عليه السلام. He (Abi Hashim) said:

I asked him about Allah - can He be described? He said: Don’t you read the Qur’an? I said: Yes (I do). He said: Don’t you read His words the Elevated: “sights do not reach Him but He reaches the sights” [6:103]? I said: Yes (I do). He said: Do you know the sights (meant)? I said: Yes. He said: What are they? I said: The sighting of the eyes. He said: The imaginings of the heart are greater than the sighting of the eyes - thus He is such that imaginations do not reach Him while He reaches the imaginations.
